field_reviews.explanation: The paper places pathway prediction inside the downstream post-training setup used for supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
The task is explicitly named pathway prediction.
The pathway prompt is grounded in the pathway network definition and gene annotations.
The route is ordinary text handled by the model's native tokenizer and consumed as text embeddings; that is the standard text path described for these backbones.
The prompt is visible to the model as tokenized text.
This is a text-native token stream with a structured biological prompt/task scaffold.
The pathway network definition and gene annotations are appended after the sequence context in the example input.
The prompt components are concatenated in order, as indicated by the text describing them as following the sequence region.
The text functions as the query/instruction asking the model to infer the biological or disease effect.
The appendix presents this as a representative input, so it is an actual model input.

supporting_quotes: "followed by a pathway network definition and gene annotations"
"The model is then asked to infer"
reviews.concise_rationale: The canonical paper gives this exact pathway-prediction example as a representative input, and the Qwen backbones are explicitly tokenizer-native. That is enough to preserve the text route as a real model input without revising the coding.
